newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ short rates end 25 bp higher after RBNZ comment.
newsitem.headline: NZ short rates end 25 bp higher after RBNZ comment.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.72 (PREV 92.88) 90-DAYS 7.10 (PREV 6.84)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.30 PCT (PREV 6.00) US 5-YR 6.53 (PREV 6.60)
* NZ 90-day rates end well above seven percent
* RBNZ calls for monetary conditions to firm somewhat
* Volumes quieten down in afternoon, market TWI watching
New Zealand short term interest rates finished 25 basis points higher on Monday following a surprise call from the central bank for firmer monetary conditions.
Key 90-day bank bills ended at 7.10 percent from their 6.84 percent finish last week, while the currency's Trade-Weighted Index was closing at 67.98 from 67.83 at Friday's close.
The TWI, which opened down at 67.4 on the back of movements in the U.S. dollar over the weekend, had recuperated to 67.65 just before the statement, after which it shot to 68.13.
Mid bonds ended 12 basis points higher in yield at 7.48 percent, while the long bond was up six to 7.64 percent.
The Reserve Bank said monetary conditions appeared to be settling at levels somewhat too low to be consistent with the intended stance of monetary policy.

"To be consistent with this stance, we would prefer to see conditions firm somewhat, to levels rather closer to the announced desired conditions," it said. The bank in March assumed a TWI at 68.0 and 90-days at 7.5 percent.

Conditions have eased substantially in the past fortnight after an interview RBNZ governor Don Brash gave, where he said the bank was reviewing the appropriateness of its assumptions, ahead of its June monetary policy statement.
One Wellington dealer said while Brash had not stated the bank would ease conditions in June, he had left a lot of scope for that interpretation.
"I wouldn't say they lead the market down the garden path but they probably started to point them that way," the dealer said.

"I think there will still be a feeling that the Reserve Bank...once they do their sums, will probably go towards easing slightly. Maybe not a heck of a lot, but they wouldn't be too happy with rates coming down a little bit.
"You'd think they'd know that now though, so the market is a little confused," he said.
